en: The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the forested mountains of Mindanao.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a two-step forward, one-step backward dance.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
Abaca is a Philippine native plant whose strong fibers are traditionally used to weave ropes and textiles.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the first two-way video telephone and discovered the law of electrical kinetic resistance.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system that uses specific curved symbols to represent spoken syllables like ka and ba.
Every Filipino citizen aged eighteen and above has the constitutional right and duty to register and vote.
The Sampaguita is the national flower of the Philippines, recognized for its highly fragrant white petals.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is a protected national park featuring a navigable underground river.
Pagmamano is a traditional Filipino gesture of respect where younger people press an elder's hand to their forehead.
